value.type: original unnormalized positive-exponent Hausdorff content H^p_δ(A), valued in [0,∞]
value.definition: For a metric space Z, A⊆Z, real p>0 and finite real δ>0, Hscale(p,δ,A), also written H^p_δ(A), is inf{∑_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^p : A⊆⋃_{i≥0}U_i, and diam U_i≤δ for all i}. Here admissible members U_i are bounded subsets of Z; their ordinary diameter is sup{dist(x,y): x,y∈U_i} in [0,∞), with diameter of ∅ equal to zero. Equivalently the memberwise admissibility condition is dist(x,y)≤δ for every x,y in each U_i. Covers are countable, represented by ℕ-indexed families, with finite covers padded by ∅, and each empty member contributes zero. No measurability, openness, or intersection-with-A restriction is imposed on cover members. All sums and infima are taken in [0,∞], and an infimum over no admissible cover is ∞. In Euclidean Z this is precisely the original formula and conventions of problem.md:34–43; the same formula defines its metric-space extension. The cutoff is ≤δ, and there is no multiplicative dimensional normalization.

value.type: original unnormalized positive-exponent Hausdorff measure H^p(A), valued in [0,∞]
value.definition: For a metric space Z, A⊆Z and real p>0, Hmeasure(p,A), also written H^p(A), is sup_{δ∈ℝ, δ>0} Hscale(p,δ,A). This is the original H^p(A)=sup_{δ>0} H^p_δ(A) of problem.md:34–43, using exactly D018's countable covers, empty-member costs and cutoff convention. It has no multiplicative normalization and is defined on every subset A, without a measurability requirement. On general metric spaces we use this same formula as the extension of the supplied Euclidean definition.

patches.old: At finite scale every nonempty cover member has finite ediam, equal to the embedding of its real diam. Since p>0, zero diameter has p-power zero; the supremum over a nonempty-member proposition is exactly that diameter power, and for an empty member it is zero. Thus the infimum in D004 is precisely the original ordinary-diameter infimum H^p_δ, and F002 identifies μH[p] with the original H^p with no factor.
patches.new: Compare with the shared original definitions D018 and D019, namely Hscale(p,δ,A)=H^p_δ(A) and Hmeasure(p,A)=H^p(A). For any fixed finite δ>0, the D004 condition ediam(U_i)≤ofReal δ is equivalent to dist(x,y)≤δ for every pair of points in U_i, by the definition of ediam as their supremum. This is exactly the D018 admissibility condition and forces each member to be bounded; conversely each D018 member of ordinary diameter ≤δ meets that extended-diameter bound. The two classes of covers therefore coincide, including empty members and empty families. On each member at this scale, finite ediam is the embedding of the ordinary supremum diameter, which also equals D003's diam; no unbounded member is admitted through toReal(∞)=0. Since p>0, zero diameter has p-power zero; the nonempty-member supremum in D004 equals the embedded diameter power on a nonempty member and is zero on an empty member, as required by D018. The same ℕ-indexed sums and infima consequently give C_p(δ,A)=Hscale(p,δ,A)=H^p_δ(A). Taking suprema over all positive finite real δ in F002 and D019 gives μH[p](A)=Hmeasure(p,A)=H^p(A). Both definitions use the cutoff ≤δ, arbitrary countable covers and no multiplicative normalization, so this comparison introduces no factor or cover restriction.
